text:
Jenna: quick summary from the continuous-batching sweep + the perf regression we saw on L4 yesterday. dumping the short findings and a proposed per-gpu cap. tl;dr: kernel selector + KV fragmentation are the root causes; we should deploy different max_batch_tokens and max_batch_size per gpu and roll canary.
Omar: can you post the p95 / throughput numbers? was this only L4 or others too?
Jenna: p95 spike was most visible on L4. under mixed-seq workload (mean seq len ~512, tails to 2048) at 100qps sustained:
- L4 (current config): p95 62ms (was 28ms), throughput -12% vs baseline
- A10: p95 34ms (no regression), throughput stable
- T4: p95 45ms (minor jitter)
- A100: p95 24ms (no regression, high occupancy)
- H100: p95 22ms
Profiling shows kernel selector falling back to a slower attention kernel once per-batch token count crosses ~96k on L4 due to workspace tiling; also memcpy pressure from fragmented KV writes.
Omar: do you have the nvprof-like breakdown?
Jenna: short dump excerpt from the run:
```
memcpy H2D: 30.2ms (25%)
attn_unfused_kernel: 22.1ms (18%)
matmul kernels: 18.4ms (15%)
kv_write + epoch-sync: 40.6ms (34%)
other: 8.7ms (8%)
```
When we cap batch_tokens to 64k on L4 the selector stays on the fused/fast kernel and p95 goes back ~30ms, throughput up ~9%.
Priya: interesting — so it's a mix of kernel-choice cliff + KV copying. is the KV copying caused by buffer fragmentation or by our slab allocator falling back to host?
Jenna: both. allocator stats show ~23% of KV allocations are served from 'fallback' slab when batch token growth is high; fallback triggers host staging buffers which cost the memcpy time above. also small-request packing increases number of kernel launches (1.8x) so warm-up cost rises.
Carlos: any quantization/compilation knock-on effects? e.g., do lower-precision kernels change threshold points?
Jenna: yes. on int8 paths, the workspace footprint is slightly smaller so threshold shifts up ~12k tokens before fallback. but int8 kernels are slower per-token for long sequences on L4 due to extra conversion steps (net win on H100/A100 though).
Omar: what's your proposed new per-gpu caps?
Jenna: proposal (config snippet below):
```
batching_heuristic:
  per_gpu:
    H100: { max_batch_size: 64, max_batch_tokens: 512000, token_budget_target: 450000 }
    A100: { max_batch_size: 48, max_batch_tokens: 256000, token_budget_target: 220000 }
    A10:  { max_batch_size: 32, max_batch_tokens: 128000, token_budget_target: 110000 }
    L4:  { max_batch_size: 16, max_batch_tokens: 64000,  token_budget_target: 55000 }
    T4:  { max_batch_size: 12, max_batch_tokens: 48000,  token_budget_target: 42000 }
  global_defaults: { max_wait_ms: 12, prefer_kernel: fused_attention }
```
Notes: token_budget_target is softer than max_batch_tokens and used by the continuous-batching pacing algorithm to decide when to flush early.
Priya: looks good. for L4 the max_batch_tokens of 64k matches the empirical cliff. do we need different settings for int8 vs fp16 models?
Jenna: yes — runtime can switch to the int8 overrides automatically (we already expose model_precision tag). suggested int8 uplift: +12k tokens for all GPUs, but reduce max_batch_size by 10% to keep kernel launch count controlled.
perf-bot: experiment artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/continuous-batching/2098765432/
perf-bot: csvs: latency_hist.csv, profile_traces.zip, allocator_stats.json, config_diff.patch
Omar: rollout plan?
Priya: start with a 10% canary on pools backing internal dev traffic, monitor p95, error-rate, kernel-selector histograms, and allocator fallback rate. if no regressions in 48h, expand to 50% then full.
Carlos: do we need any changes to the kernel selector heuristics or just the caps?
Jenna: short-term => caps. long-term => we should make the kernel selector workspace-aware (pick kernel with simulated tiling cost + kv-mem pressure prediction). also add a 'force_fused' override for critical routes.
infra-bot: deploying canary group: deployment id rwd-batchcaps-2098765432 -> 10% (dev pool) :rocket:
Omar: add a dashboard panel for allocator fallback rate and kernel_choice_ratio, please.
Priya: will add. alert if allocator_fallback_rate > 5% for 5m or kernel_choice_ratio (fused/total) drops below 0.7.
Jenna: thanks — I'll update the runtime config PR with these per-gpu values and include the int8 uplift. leaving notes in the experiment dir. next steps: small canary, monitor, iterate selector long-term.
Carlos: ack :thumbsup:
Jenna: thanks everyone.
